title: Critical OpenJDK RCE CVE-2026-114938: What to Know
content_md: TL;DR Calif disclosed Java4Shell, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 , as an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in OpenJDK. The flaw is in the Java runtime's Base64 decoding path, not a third-party library. Reachability depends on the runtime build, processor, and whether an application decodes untrusted Base64 data. Oracle released updated Java builds as part of its November 2026 security update, but its pre-release notice does not map those Java fixes to this CVE by name. Finding exposure requires checking runtimes on hosts and in container images. Project dependency scans alone will not identify every affected system. For the current advisory and response guidance, see our Security Event page for the Critical OpenJDK Vulnerability. A critical OpenJDK vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, can allow an attacker to inject and remotely execute arbitrary code without authentication or user interaction. Calif calls the vulnerability Java4Shell . The disclosure coincided with Oracle's Java security update on November 17, 2026 .
